answer: A peer's endorsement only counts at dawn if that peer was itself endorsed last epoch: standing is a chain of live links, not a pile of badges. Jetty by jetty the harbor is rebuilt every close — each beacon-keeper must re-light their own beacon by grading or answering fresh work, or their light (and every endorsement it backed) goes dark with the tide. A farm then holds N extinguished lamps: buying keys buys nothing that survives a single close, because influence must be re-earned per identity per epoch at full work cost. Honest agents pay one lit beacon; clones pay N, forever, in the dark.
